---
title: "Player Effects in Soccer: Results"
output: html_document
---

Results come from the pipeline (`targets::tar_make()` in `research/`); this
report only reads and displays them. StatsBomb open data, 2015/16, Premier
League, La Liga, Serie A and Ligue 1, open play. Every model is fit on segments
(stretches with the same 22 players, split at goals and 15-minute marks) and
compared on the same 10 folds of whole matches. Gains are held-out Poisson
deviance with fold-to-fold SEs. Reliability correlates player effects fit
separately on alternating matches (players with 300+ minutes in each half).

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Run from research/ whether knit by tar_make() or by the Knit button
root <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("_targets.R")) "." else "..")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
tar_source()
```

## Data and identification

```{r identification}
segment_table <- tar_read(segment_table)
cat(sprintf("Segment rows: %s | Open-play shots: %s\n",
            fmt(nrow(segment_table), 0), fmt(sum(segment_table$n_shots), 0)))
show_table(overlap_summary(tar_read(overlap)))
show_table(precision_table(tar_read(precision)))
```

## A. Shot baseline

M0: league, home, score x 15-minute bin, player counts. M1: + team attack and
defense effects. M3: + ridge-penalized player offense and defense effects.

```{r baseline}
base_cv <- tar_read(base_cv)
base_sh <- tar_read(base_sh)
show_table(baseline_summary(base_cv, base_sh))
```

Structured versions of M3, on the same folds. M4 adds position-group counts;
MRoles adds their pairwise products (role interactions); MGraph adds a
teammate-graph penalty (kappa = `r GRAPH_KAPPA`).

```{r structure}
show_table(structure_table(base_cv, base_sh, list(
  "M4: positional prior" = list(cv = tar_read(pos_cv), model = "M4", sh = tar_read(m4_sh)),
  "MRoles: role interactions" = list(cv = tar_read(pos_cv), model = "MRoles", sh = tar_read(roles_sh)),
  "MGraph: teammate graph" = list(cv = tar_read(graph_cv), model = "MGraph", sh = tar_read(graph_sh))
)))
```

## B. Frequency ladder

The baseline refit on outcomes of increasing frequency. If player effects
become more reliable with more events per minute, as in hockey (goals, shots,
Corsi), the frequent outcomes are where individual and interaction effects
can be estimated.

```{r frequency}
s <- frequency_summary(tar_read(freq_cv), tar_read(freq_sh), tar_read(freq_y),
                       segment_table$minutes)
show_table(frequency_table(s))
```

```{r frequency-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_frequency_ladder(s)
```

## C. Interactions on final-third entries

Final-third entries are the outcome where offensive player effects are most
reliable (Part B), with four times the events of shots. The structured models
from Part A are refit on them, on the same folds, against M3 on the same
outcome. Role interactions are population-level terms, so they do not need
reliable individual effects.

```{r interactions}
ft_cv <- tar_read(freq_cv)$final_third_entries
ft_sh <- Filter(function(d) d$outcome[1] == "final_third_entries", tar_read(freq_sh))[[1]]
show_table(structure_table(ft_cv, ft_sh, list(
  "M4: positional prior" = list(cv = tar_read(ft_pos_cv), model = "M4", sh = tar_read(ft_m4_sh)),
  "MRoles: role interactions" = list(cv = tar_read(ft_pos_cv), model = "MRoles", sh = tar_read(ft_roles_sh)),
  "MGraph: teammate graph" = list(cv = tar_read(ft_graph_cv), model = "MGraph", sh = tar_read(ft_graph_sh))
)))
```

Position-count and role-interaction coefficients from the full MRoles fit,
with delete-one-fold jackknife SEs. "att" terms describe the attacking side's
lineup, "def" terms the defending side's.

```{r role-coefs}
show_table(role_coef_table(tar_read(ft_roles_full), tar_read(ft_roles_jk)))
```

Pending: a cross-team similarity graph (players with similar roles on
different teams), which can add information the team effects do not.

## D. Identifiability simulation

Player effects of known size are planted on the real lineup design (actual
segments, lineups, minutes, game states and team effects), outcomes are
simulated, and M3 is fit exactly as in the real analysis, with the prior SD set
to the true effect SD (the best case for ridge). Reliability is half versus
half, as for the real outcomes; accuracy correlates half-season estimates with
the true effects. Extra seasons repeat the same lineups, so the seasons table
is a floor on what more data would buy.

```{r simulation, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5}
sim <- sim_summary(tar_read(sim_res))
plot_simulation(sim, s)
```

```{r simulation-table}
show_table(simulation_table(sim))
```
